title: Energy Stores and Transfers (KS4 Physics)
subject: Physics
strapline: Where energy is stored, how it moves, and conservation.
facts: Energy is stored in different stores: kinetic, gravitational potential, elastic, thermal, chemical, nuclear, magnetic and electrostatic.
Energy is transferred between stores mechanically, electrically, by heating, or by radiation (light/sound).
The principle of conservation of energy: energy cannot be created or destroyed, only transferred or stored.
Kinetic energy = ½ × mass × velocity² (Eₖ = ½mv²).
Gravitational potential energy = mass × gravitational field strength × height (Eₚ = mgh).
In real systems some energy is dissipated (wasted), usually as thermal energy to the surroundings.
Efficiency = useful energy output ÷ total energy input (× 100 for a percentage).

quick_quiz.q: Can energy be created or destroyed?
A moving car has which energy store?

quick_quiz.a: useful energy out ÷ total energy in

teacher_tips: Use "stores and transfers" language precisely — GCSE marks depend on it.
Track energy through a Sankey diagram to show waste.
Avoid the old "types of energy" phrasing; it is now stores.
